transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I... well, I came in because I keep thinking it would be better if I just didn't wake up. Like, sometimes I feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew. I've been doing flooring for over twenty years, you know? Started right after I dropped out of college. My knees are completely shot from all the tile and carpet work. It's funny how you don't think about your knees when you're twenty, but now every time I kneel on that concrete, I feel it right up into my hips. I tried those gel pads, but they slip around too much when you're trying to stretch carpet. My foreman, Dave, he always says I should just get the surgery, but who has time for that? Anyway... yeah, I just feel like I deserve to die for everything I've ruined.
How long have you been feeling like you deserve to die?

It's been... about a year and two months, I think. Yeah, it really settled in a few months after my husband's injury. When he got hurt, everything just kind of... well, dealing with the insurance companies is a full-time job on its own. They put you on hold forever. I remember I was sitting in my truck outside this dentist's office we were working on, just listening to that awful elevator music on the phone for two hours. We were ripping out all their old linoleum. Have you ever noticed how medical offices always have that same ugly, speckled blue flooring? The adhesive they used under it back in the day is like literal cement. I had to use this heavy-duty floor scraper, and my hands were cramping so bad by the end of the day, I could barely even hold my steering wheel to drive home...
Do you still find pleasure in the things you used to enjoy?

No... not really. I used to do a lot, actually. I'd paint, cook these really big meals, go for a run before heading to a job... I even used to show up for community theater rehearsals. But now all of that... it just feels like chores from somebody else's life, you know? I don't even care if I miss them anymore. 

Like the running... I used to run down by the river trail, right behind that massive new condo complex they just put up. We actually bid on the flooring contract for that place. Three hundred units, all needing luxury vinyl plank. LVP is everywhere now. People think it looks just like real hardwood, but it doesn't sound right when you walk on it. It has this hollow click-clack sound, especially if you don't use the right underlayment. And the snap-together edges are so brittle, if the subfloor isn't perfectly level, they just snap right off when you try to lock them in. We spent a whole week once just pouring self-leveling compound in this one lady's house because her foundation settled, and the smell of that stuff... it just clings to your clothes for days, no matter how much you wash them in hot water. 

But um... what were you asking? Oh, right, enjoying things. Yeah, no, I just don't have it in me to care about any of my old stuff.
You mentioned feeling like you deserve to die for what you've done to your family and crew, can you tell me more about what you've done that's causing you to feel this way?

I just... I keep thinking I'm the reason my husband got worse. And the crew lost work, and clients' homes got messed up... it's like I poisoned everything I touched. Like, I really believe I deserve whatever happens to me now. 

There was this one client's house, we were doing a custom shower pan. You have to get the slope exactly right, a quarter inch per foot down towards the drain, or the water just sits there and breeds mold. We use this dry-pack mortar, deck mud they call it. It’s mostly sand with just a little Portland cement, and you have to pack it down so tight. I was using my magnesium float, trying to get the pitch perfect, but... water damage is no joke, you know? Once it gets into the studs, you're looking at thousands of dollars in rot repair. I saw a house once where the termites had come up through the slab because of a slow leak in a shower pan, and they ate the entire bottom plate of the framing. You could literally push your finger through the wood like it was wet cardboard. It's terrifying how fast a house can just rot from the inside out. Just completely destroyed because of one mistake under the tile. 

But... yeah. I just... I ruin things. I poisoned my husband's recovery, I messed up the jobs for my crew... I just deserve the worst.
Can you tell me more about what you think you did to poison your husband's recovery?

Well, it's just... I wasn't there enough, mentally, you know? After he got hurt, he needed me to be strong, to handle the business and the house, but I just... I couldn't keep it together. I was so distracted, so useless. I'd forget his appointments, or I'd snap at him because I was stressed about money. It's like my bad energy just seeped into him and made his pain worse. 

And then with the crew... I'd mess up the measurements for the jobs. Like, we were doing this huge commercial carpet installation for a hotel lobby. Broadloom carpet, the really heavy stuff with the intricate patterns that you have to match up perfectly at the seams. You have to use a power stretcher to get it tight, otherwise it ripples after a few months of foot traffic. And the seaming iron... you have to let it get to exactly the right temperature, or the thermoplastic tape won't melt right, and the seam will split open right in the middle of the hallway. I burned my forearm on one of those irons once, right through my long sleeve shirt. The scar looks like a little crescent moon. I used to tell my niece it was a burn from a shooting star when she was little. She's in middle school now, playing the flute in the marching band. They practice so early in the morning, I don't know how those kids function. 

But... yeah, the hotel job. I ordered the wrong dye lot for half the rolls, and it was so obvious once we rolled it out. The crew lost three days of pay because we had to wait for the replacement, and the general contractor was furious. I just... I ruin everything. My husband, the crew, the clients' homes... it's all my fault. I poisoned it all, and I really do deserve whatever bad things come my way.
Can you tell me more about what specifically makes you feel guilty about your husband's injury?

It's just... I really believe I'm the reason he got worse after it happened. Like I said, I just... I poisoned everything I touched. He was trying so hard to recover, and I was just this dark cloud over him, making everything harder. And it wasn't just him, it was the crew losing work, and the clients' homes getting messed up... I just ruined it all. I really think I deserve whatever happens to me now. 

Like when we were doing that tile job in the master bath for that nice older couple... we were installing this beautiful glass mosaic accent border. Glass tile is so tricky, you know? You can't use regular thinset mortar because it'll show through the translucent glass and ruin the color. You have to use this special bright white, highly modified thinset, and you have to knock down the trowel ridges perfectly flat before you set the sheets, otherwise you see these ugly gray lines behind the tile. And cutting it... you need a special glass blade on the wet saw, and even then, it chips so easily. I spent three hours one afternoon just trying to get one perfectly clean cut around a shower valve. The water from the wet saw is always freezing cold, too. It sprays all over your shirt and your safety glasses get fogged up. I usually wear those yellow-tinted safety glasses because they make everything look a little brighter, especially when you're working in a basement with no windows. Basements always smell like damp earth and old cardboard boxes. 

But... yeah, I just... I'm the reason everything went wrong for him. For everyone. I deserve to be punished for it.
Have you thought about how you would carry out this punishment, or dying, that you feel you deserve?

I just... I came in here because I keep thinking it would be better if I didn't wake up. Like, sometimes I feel like dying would just be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew. I don't have a specific plan or anything, just this heavy feeling that I shouldn't be here anymore. 

It's like when you're installing sheet vinyl, you know? The big rolls. If you don't acclimate it to the room temperature for at least 24 hours before you cut it, it shrinks. I learned that the hard way when I was an apprentice. We rolled out this beautiful faux-wood vinyl in a kitchen, glued it down, and the next day it had pulled away from the baseboards by almost half an inch. You can't stretch it back. Once it's cut and glued, it's done. You have to rip the whole thing up, scrape the adhesive off the subfloor, and start over. Scraping adhesive is the absolute worst. You have to use these long-handled razor scrapers, and you're on your hands and knees for hours. My knees are completely shot from this job. Even with the good gel kneepads, the ones with the hard plastic caps that let you swivel on the floor... after twenty years, the cartilage just wears away. My doctor told me I should take glucosamine, but those pills are huge. They look like horse pills. I can never swallow them without gagging. 

But yeah... I just feel like it would be better if I just went to sleep and didn't wake up. It would just be fair.
Have you thought about how you would end your life if you decided to go through with it?

Well, like I was saying... I don't really have a plan, exactly. I just came in because I keep thinking it would be better if I didn't wake up. Like, sometimes I feel like dying would just be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew. It's just this constant thought, you know? 

Like a bad seam in a carpet that you can't stop staring at. Once you see it, it's all you can see. And seaming is an art, really. You have to use a row finder to separate the tufts of the carpet perfectly so you don't cut any of the yarn. If you cut the yarn, it frays, and the seam looks terrible. And you have to use a special latex seam sealer on the raw edges before you iron it together. It smells awful, like sour milk and chemicals. I spilled a whole bottle of it in my truck once, right on the passenger seat. My truck still smells like it on hot days. It's a Ford F-150, an older model, but it's got the extended cab so I can fit all my tools in the back. The air conditioning went out last summer, and driving around with the windows down just blows dust everywhere. My husband used to fix the truck for me. He was always so good with engines. He could just listen to a car and know exactly what was wrong with it... 

But, yeah. I don't have a plan. I just think it would be better if I didn't wake up. It's just what I deserve.
Have you ever thought of a specific way you would end your life?

I... I know you keep asking that, but I really don't have a specific way picked out. I just... I came in because I keep thinking it would be better if I didn't wake up. Like, sometimes I feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew. I just want to go to sleep and have it all stop. 

Sleep is so hard to come by anyway. When you do flooring, your back just aches all night. You get these knots right between your shoulder blades from carrying boxes of tile. A box of ceramic tile can weigh fifty pounds, and you're carrying them up stairs, down hallways... My chiropractor said I have the spine of an eighty-year-old. His office always has this really soothing music playing, like pan flutes or something. And they have a little water fountain in the waiting room. I tried to buy one of those tabletop fountains for my living room once, thinking it would help me relax. But the pump was too loud. It just hummed this annoying, low pitch that gave me a headache. It sounded like the refrigerator when the compressor kicks on. Our fridge is so old, it makes a terrible racket. I keep telling myself I'll buy a new one, maybe one of those stainless steel ones with the ice maker in the door. I always wanted an ice maker in the door...

But no, I don't have a plan. I just think dying is what I deserve.
Have you felt this way, like you deserve to die, nearly every day since your husband's injury?

Yeah, almost every day. It didn't start the exact day he got hurt, though. It was maybe a few months after his injury when it really set in. So this depression has been with me for about a year and two months now. 

A year and two months... that was right around when the weather started turning cold. I hate the cold weather. When you're cutting tile outside on the wet saw in the winter, your hands just absolutely freeze. The water sprays back at you, and even if you wear those thick rubber gloves, the chill just seeps right into your bones. I bought these expensive heated gloves online once, the kind that run on a little rechargeable battery pack you tuck into the wrist. They worked great for exactly one week before the charger just stopped working. Everything is made so cheap these days. You buy a power tool now, and it's got plastic gears inside instead of metal. My dad had a drill from the seventies, all metal casing, weighed like ten pounds. You could drop that thing off a roof and it would still work perfectly. He used to build birdhouses with it out in the garage. He loved birds. We had this big cedar feeder in the backyard that attracted blue jays and cardinals, but the squirrels kept stealing all the black oil sunflower seed. Squirrels are so smart, they figure out every baffle and trick you try to use to keep them away... 

But anyway, yeah. It's been about a year and two months of feeling like this.
Have you experienced significant weight loss or gain since you started feeling this way?

Well, I guess I've lost some weight, yeah. Most days I just forget to eat until it's really late, or I'll take a few bites of something and just feel sick to my stomach. I'm definitely not trying to lose weight, but my work pants have gotten really loose lately. 

I actually had to buy a new belt last week. It's this thick leather one, really sturdy. You need a good belt when you wear a tool pouch all day. My old tool pouch was made of canvas, and it just fell apart after a couple of years. The seams ripped right where I kept my utility knife. A good utility knife is so important. You have to change the blades constantly if you want a clean cut on carpet, otherwise you get those fuzzy edges. I buy the blades in bulk, those big dispensers of a hundred blades. They come coated in this thin layer of oil so they don't rust in the package. I hate the smell of that oil. It gets on your fingers and you can't wash it off, even with that gritty orange soap mechanics use. My husband used to use that soap all the time. His hands were always so rough, but he could fix anything... 

But yeah, my pants are definitely looser now. I just don't have an appetite anymore.
Have you had periods of feeling better in between times when you felt like you deserved to die?

Well, I guess... there was a stretch of several weeks where I was actually getting up in the morning, you know? I was eating a little better, not crying all day long. But... I still heard the voice when I was at work, and I was still completely convinced that the clients and the suppliers were tracking me. 

The suppliers are always watching everything anyway. When you go into the flooring distributor to pick up an order, they have these big security cameras pointing right at the loading dock. They say it's to prevent theft, because pallets of luxury vinyl plank are pretty expensive. That stuff has gotten so popular lately. Everyone wants it because it looks like real wood but it's waterproof. You can put it right in a bathroom or a basement. We did a basement job last spring where the floor was so uneven, we had to pour self-leveling compound over the whole thing before we could even start. That compound is tricky to work with, it sets up so fast. You have to mix it in these big buckets with a heavy-duty paddle mixer. If you don't clean the paddle right away, the concrete just dries on there like a rock and ruins it. I ruined a really good mixer that way once. It was a Makita. They make good tools, usually... 

But yeah, even when I wasn't crying all day for those few weeks, I still knew they were tracking me, and the voice was still there.
Are there any days when you don't feel like you deserve to die?

Not really, no. I mean, for most of the time since this all started, the guilt, the exhaustion, the not caring about anything, and just... thinking I should be dead... it's all just been there. Even if some weeks were a little less crushing than others, it never really goes away. 

It's like that dust you get when you're tearing up old ceramic tile. You can tape off the doorways with plastic sheeting, you can run an air scrubber, you can wear a respirator, but that fine white dust just gets everywhere. It settles on the baseboards, it gets into the HVAC vents, it coats your eyelashes. And you think you've cleaned it all up, you mop the floors three times, but the next day you walk in and there's this hazy white film on everything again. It's impossible to get rid of. We had a client once who was so mad about the dust, she threatened to withhold our final payment. She had these expensive velvet couches that she refused to move out of the living room before we started demo. Velvet is the worst fabric for holding onto dust. It's like a magnet. My grandmother had a velvet armchair, this dark emerald green color. She used to sit in it and knit these itchy wool sweaters for us every Christmas. I always hated wearing them, but I smiled and put them on anyway because she looked so proud. She passed away a long time ago, though... 

But anyway, yeah. Most of the time, the guilt and the thoughts about dying are just always there.
Do you feel like you deserve to die every single day, or are there some days when you don't think about it as much?

Well, I guess... I guess it's pretty much every day. That's actually why I came in. I just keep thinking it would be so much better if I went to sleep and didn't wake up. It feels like dying would be a fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew. 

My crew... they've been trying to cover for me, I know they have. Taking on extra jobs, working late. We have this one guy, Tommy, he's only twenty-two but he works like a machine. He can carry two bundles of laminate flooring up a flight of stairs without even breathing hard. Those bundles are heavy, too, usually around thirty or forty pounds each depending on the thickness of the planks. We always try to get the 12-millimeter ones because they feel more like real hardwood when you walk on them. The thinner ones sound hollow, you know? Unless you use a really good underlayment. The underlayment is crucial. You can get the kind with the built-in vapor barrier, which you absolutely need if you're installing over a concrete subfloor, otherwise moisture seeps up and warps the boards. I saw a floor completely buckle once because the previous installer skipped the vapor barrier to save a few bucks. It looked like a roller coaster. We had to rip the whole thing out. Pulling up ruined flooring is the worst job, you never know what you're going to find underneath. Sometimes it's just mold, sometimes it's old linoleum from the seventies with asbestos in the adhesive... 

But yeah, I... I just feel like I deserve to die for putting everyone through this. Every day.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

I don't... no, not really. I used to do a lot of things. I used to paint, I'd cook these big meals for everyone, I'd even go for a run before heading out to a job site. I was involved in local theater, too, always showing up for rehearsals. But now... all of that just feels like chores from somebody else's life. I don't even care if I miss rehearsals anymore. 

Theater is a lot of work, though. People don't realize how much goes into building the sets. We did a production of 'Death of a Salesman' a few years ago, and I volunteered to do the floors for the Loman house set. We used this really cheap peel-and-stick vinyl because it's just for a stage, it doesn't need to last twenty years. But the adhesive on those cheap tiles is terrible. If the stage lights get too hot, the glue softens and the tiles start sliding around. We had one actor almost trip during a really dramatic monologue because a tile had shifted. It was a disaster. Stage lighting is so incredibly hot, especially the older incandescent fixtures. They draw so much power, too. You have to be really careful about not overloading the circuits. My uncle was an electrician, he used to tell me horror stories about people plugging too many space heaters into one outlet and burning their houses down. He was always so paranoid about fire safety. He used to test his smoke alarms every single week. He'd walk around the house with a broom handle and poke the little button on each one... 

But yeah, I don't do any of those things anymore. I just don't have the energy or the interest. None of it matters.
Has your feeling of deserving to die been present nearly every day since it started about a year and two months ago?

Yeah, it has. It's been with me for about a year and two months now... it started a few months after my husband's injury. Since then, it's just been this constant weight. Every day. 

His injury... it was a bad one. He was helping me load some heavy rolls of carpet into the back of the van, and he just moved wrong. Carpet is deceivingly heavy, especially the high-pile plush stuff. People always want that really thick, soft carpet for their bedrooms, the kind that feels like walking on a cloud. But they don't realize how dense it is. A standard 12-foot roll can weigh hundreds of pounds. You have to use a carpet dolly to move it, you can't just carry it. We usually try to get the supplier to cut it into smaller room-sized pieces before we pick it up, but sometimes they mess up the order or their cutting machine is down. Their cutting machines are massive, they take up half the warehouse. I always wondered how they sharpen the blades on those things. It must be a specialized service that comes in, like the guys who sharpen the knives for professional kitchens. My sister used to date a chef, and he was obsessed with his knives. He had this leather roll he kept them in, and he wouldn't let anyone else wash them. He'd spend hours on Sunday afternoons just running them over a whetstone... 

But, um, yes. To answer your question, the feeling has been there pretty much every day for a year and two months.
Are there any small things that still bring you joy or pleasure?

No... no, not even the small things. Like I said before, I used to do all sorts of stuff. I used to paint... I'd cook these big meals for everyone, I'd go for a run before heading out to a job site. I was always showing up for my theater rehearsals, too. But now, it's just... none of it. Those things feel like chores from somebody else's life. I don't even care if I miss rehearsals anymore. 

Theater used to be such a big part of my life, you know? The smell of the sawdust in the scene shop... we had this massive table saw, an old Delta Unisaw. It was a beast. You had to respect it, or it would take a finger right off. We always made sure the blade guard was down, and we used push sticks. I made my own push stick out of a scrap piece of oak. Hardwoods are better for push sticks because they don't splinter as easily if you accidentally nick them with the blade. Oak is incredibly dense. We did a solid oak floor for this old Victorian house once, the planks were almost an inch thick. We had to use a special pneumatic nailer, the kind you hit with a heavy mallet to drive the cleat in. It's exhausting work, swinging that mallet all day. Your arm feels like it's going to fall off by the end of the week. You have to ice your shoulder every night. My husband used to make these ice packs out of rubbing alcohol and water in a Ziploc bag, so they'd get super cold but stay slushy and mold to your joint... 

But no, I don't get joy from anything anymore. It's all just gone.
Are your feelings of deserving to die more related to specific things you've done or to a general feeling about yourself?

It's... it's specific things I've done. I just keep thinking I'm the reason my husband got worse. And why the crew lost work, and how clients' homes got messed up... I feel like I just poisoned everything I touched, so I deserve whatever happens to me. 

But speaking of clients' homes, we were doing this custom tile job in a master bathroom right before things got really bad. Carrara marble. It's beautiful stuff, but it stains if you even look at it wrong. You have to seal it before you grout, otherwise the grout haze gets trapped in the pores of the stone. Grout is basically just colored cement, you know? It's crazy how fast it sets up if you mix it too warm. We had this guy on the crew, Dave, who would always mix the grout with hot water from the client's tap because he didn't want to walk out to the hose in the winter. Hot water makes the chemical reaction happen twice as fast. We ended up having to chisel out an entire shower pan because it hardened before we could wash it off. Chiseling grout is the worst sound in the world, it's like nails on a chalkboard but amplified. My dog hates high-pitched noises like that. He's a rescue, a terrier mix. He used to hide under the bed whenever the vacuum cleaner came out. Vacuums have those really high-pitched whines from the motor bearings. You have to replace the filters on those things all the time or the motor burns out. I used to buy the HEPA filters in bulk online... 

But... yeah. I just feel like I ruined everything for everyone. I deserve it.
Have your feelings of deserving to die changed in intensity or frequency at all since they started?

No, they haven't really changed. It's just... I came in because I keep thinking it would be better if I didn't wake up, and sometimes I feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew. It's just this constant drumbeat in my head. 

Speaking of drumbeats, my nephew started taking drum lessons a few months ago. My sister is losing her mind because he practices all afternoon. She tried putting soundproofing foam on the walls of his bedroom, but that egg-crate foam doesn't actually block sound, it just stops it from echoing. If you want to actually soundproof a room, you need mass. You have to use something like mass-loaded vinyl or double layers of drywall with green glue in between. Green glue is this special acoustic compound that stays flexible so it absorbs the sound vibrations. It comes in these big tubes, like caulking. Caulking is another thing people mess up all the time. They use 100% silicone in places they want to paint, and paint won't stick to silicone. You have to use a siliconized acrylic blend if you want to paint it. I always kept a wet rag on me when I was caulking baseboards, to smooth the bead out. You have to keep your finger wet or it drags... 

But, um... yeah. The feeling of wanting to just not wake up... it's always there. It hasn't let up.
Have your feelings of deserving to die remained the same since they started about a year and two months ago?

Yeah, I mean... the depression, that heavy feeling, it's been with me for about a year and two months now. It started a few months after my husband's injury. It's just been dragging on ever since. 

Injuries are so tough, you know? Especially back injuries. The spine is just this incredibly complex stack of bones and nerves, and once it's out of whack, everything else goes with it. We had a guy on a job site once who herniated a disc just lifting a box of ceramic tiles. Ceramic is heavy, but porcelain is even denser. Porcelain is baked at a much higher temperature, so it absorbs less water. That's why you have to use it outdoors if you live somewhere that freezes, otherwise the tiles absorb moisture and crack when the water expands into ice. Ice expansion is actually how potholes form in the roads every winter. The water gets into the asphalt, freezes, pushes the pavement up, and then when it melts, there's a void underneath and the road collapses under the weight of the cars. The city is always patching them with that cold-patch asphalt, but it never lasts. You really need to heat up the edges of the hole with a torch to get the new asphalt to bond properly. We used a propane torch once to melt adhesive off a concrete slab before laying new carpet...

But, yeah. A year and two months. It hasn't changed. Just this constant weight since a few months after he got hurt.

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep thinking I'm the reason my husband got worse, the crew lost work, and clients' homes got messed up, like I poisoned everything I touched and deserve whatever happens to me.

patient.answer:
I just... I keep thinking I'm the reason my husband got worse. And the crew lost work, and clients' homes got messed up... it's like I poisoned everything I touched. Like, I really believe I deserve whatever happens to me now. 

There was this one client's house, we were doing a custom shower pan. You have to get the slope exactly right, a quarter inch per foot down towards the drain, or the water just sits there and breeds mold. We use this dry-pack mortar, deck mud they call it. It’s mostly sand with just a little Portland cement, and you have to pack it down so tight. I was using my magnesium float, trying to get the pitch perfect, but... water damage is no joke, you know? Once it gets into the studs, you're looking at thousands of dollars in rot repair. I saw a house once where the termites had come up through the slab because of a slow leak in a shower pan, and they ate the entire bottom plate of the framing. You could literally push your finger through the wood like it was wet cardboard. It's terrifying how fast a house can just rot from the inside out. Just completely destroyed because of one mistake under the tile. 

But... yeah. I just... I ruin things. I poisoned my husband's recovery, I messed up the jobs for my crew... I just deserve the worst.

And then with the crew... I'd mess up the measurements for the jobs. Like, we were doing this huge commercial carpet installation for a hotel lobby. Broadloom carpet, the really heavy stuff with the intricate patterns that you have to match up perfectly at the seams. And the seaming iron... you have to let it get to exactly the right temperature, or the thermoplastic tape won't melt right, and the seam will split open right in the middle of the hallway. I burned my forearm on one of those irons once, right through my long sleeve shirt. The scar looks like a little crescent moon. I used to tell my niece it was a burn from a shooting star when she was little. She's in middle school now, playing the flute in the marching band. They practice so early in the morning, I don't know how those kids function. 

But... yeah, the hotel job. I ordered the wrong dye lot for half the rolls, and it was so obvious once we rolled it out. The crew lost three days of pay because we had to wait for the replacement, and the general contractor was furious. I just... I ruin everything. My husband, the crew, the clients' homes... it's all my fault. I poisoned it all, and I really do deserve whatever bad things come my way.

patient.answer:
No, they haven't really changed. It's just... I came in because I keep thinking it would be better if I didn't wake up, and sometimes I feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew. It's just this constant drumbeat in my head. 

Speaking of drumbeats, my nephew started taking drum lessons a few months ago. My sister is losing her mind because he practices all afternoon. She tried putting soundproofing foam on the walls of his bedroom, but that egg-crate foam doesn't actually block sound, it just stops it from echoing. If you want to actually soundproof a room, you need mass. You have to use something like mass-loaded vinyl or double layers of drywall with green glue in between. Green glue is this special acoustic compound that stays flexible so it absorbs the sound vibrations. It comes in these big tubes, like caulking. Caulking is another thing people mess up all the time. They use 100% silicone in places they want to paint, and paint won't stick to silicone. You have to use a siliconized acrylic blend if you want to paint it. I always kept a wet rag on me when I was caulking baseboards, to smooth the bead out. You have to keep your finger wet or it drags... 

But, um... yeah. The feeling of wanting to just not wake up... it's always there. It hasn't let up.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's feelings of deserving to die are persistent and unchanged over the past year and two months
doctor.question: Have your feelings of deserving to die remained the same since they started about a year and two months ago?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depression has been with me for about a year and two months, since a few months after my husband's injury.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of the patient's depressive symptoms (feelings of deserving to die), specifically referencing the 1 year and 2 months timeframe.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I mean... the depression, that heavy feeling, it's been with me for about a year and two months now. It started a few months after my husband's injury. It's just been dragging on ever since. 

Injuries are so tough, you know? Especially back injuries. The spine is just this incredibly complex stack of bones and nerves, and once it's out of whack, everything else goes with it. We had a guy on a job site once who herniated a disc just lifting a box of ceramic tiles. Ceramic is heavy, but porcelain is even denser. Porcelain is baked at a much higher temperature, so it absorbs less water. That's why you have to use it outdoors if you live somewhere that freezes, otherwise the tiles absorb moisture and crack when the water expands into ice. Ice expansion is actually how potholes form in the roads every winter. The water gets into the asphalt, freezes, pushes the pavement up, and then when it melts, there's a void underneath and the road collapses under the weight of the cars. The city is always patching them with that cold-patch asphalt, but it never lasts. You really need to heat up the edges of the hole with a torch to get the new asphalt to bond properly. We used a propane torch once to melt adhesive off a concrete slab before laying new carpet...

But, yeah. A year and two months. It hasn't changed. Just this constant weight since a few months after he got hurt.
